identity.title: Improving Diffusion Models for Class-imbalanced Training Data via Capacity Manipulation

problem.claim: Diffusion models can degrade substantially on minority classes when trained on imbalanced datasets.

gap.claim: Model capacity allocation is presented as a previously underexplored factor, distinct from existing research, in explaining this issue.

contributions.claim: The authors report that majority classes use an unnecessarily large share of model capacity, limiting minority-class representation.
Capacity Manipulation (CM) reserves capacity for minority classes using low-rank parameter decomposition and a capacity manipulation loss.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their perspective by treating model capacity allocation as an orthogonal factor in class-imbalanced diffusion-model training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that empirical experiments and theoretical analysis support majority-class capacity monopolization as a restriction on minority representation.
The authors report that extensive experiments show CM consistently and significantly improves diffusion-model robustness on imbalanced datasets.
The authors report further overall-performance gains when CM is combined with existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Imbalanced training data can cause diffusion models to perform poorly on minority classes.
The authors identify capacity allocation as an underexplored, orthogonal perspective and report majority-class overuse of capacity.
CM explicitly reserves capacity for minority knowledge through low-rank parameterization and a dedicated loss.
Experiments are reported to show improved robustness and additional gains alongside existing methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a resource-allocation diagnosis—majority classes occupying excess capacity—to a method that explicitly reserves capacity for minority classes.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make its intervention legible by aligning the mechanism directly with the diagnosed bottleneck.
lessons.application: Frame a proposed method as an explicit resource or constraint adjustment that targets the limiting factor identified in the analysis.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the abstract does not establish a concrete bottleneck or when the intervention addresses a different mechanism.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, effect sizes, or experimental settings.
The theoretical analysis' assumptions and formal results are not given.
The relative contribution of CM versus combining it with existing methods is unspecified.
